_meta.purpose: Reference property corpus for the PropertyGPT-style retrieval stage. For a contract with zero transaction history, we substitute 'properties humans have already written' for 'transactions we could have mined', and hand the retrieved ones to the model as in-context examples.
_meta.provenance: The category taxonomy follows Trace2Inv's eight invariant categories; the property statements imitate the style of Certora audit reports. This corpus was written by hand — it is NOT an embedding of real Certora reports. See the limitations section of the README.
_meta.retrieval: Lexical retrieval over static signals, not embedding similarity. Deterministic and runnable offline with no API key, which suits a demo; it does not generalize semantically, which is its main weakness.

signals.erc777_hook: ERC777 / ERC1820 / tokensReceived / tokensToSend — a recipient callback hook exists
signals.external_call_before_state_write: An external call precedes a state variable update inside a function body (CEI violation)
signals.no_reentrancy_guard: No nonReentrant / ReentrancyGuard anywhere in the source
signals.per_account_cap: A mapping(address => uint256) accumulator compared against a constant cap
signals.price_oracle: getPrice / oracle / getReserves / latestAnswer — an external price source
signals.payable_receive: receive() external payable, or a payable function

properties.statement: No externally reachable function may be reentered before its own execution completes. Reentrancy depth must be zero on entry.
properties.why: Where a recipient callback exists (ERC777 tokensReceived, ERC721 onERC721Received, ETH receive), control passes to the attacker at the external call site.

properties.statement: At the moment a function performs an external call, every state variable that function is responsible for updating must already be updated.
properties.why: A CEI violation lets a reentrant call read stale state, so the same require check passes more than once.

properties.statement: Cumulative allocation per account may never exceed the declared per-account cap, including after any transaction completes.
properties.why: A require check only inspects the value at function entry. The cap is a post-condition that must also hold at transaction end.

properties.statement: The total recorded in the contract's internal ledger must always equal the total value that has actually left the contract.
properties.why: A divergence between ledger and reality means funds have already over-flowed, or the accounting has been manipulated.

properties.statement: An accumulating counter must increase monotonically, and its increase within a single transaction may not exceed the amount that transaction requested.
properties.why: Reentrancy increments the counter several times inside one external transaction, breaking exactly this property.

properties.statement: Gas consumption on the normal-use path stays below a fixed bound.
properties.why: Part of the combination that blocked 23 of 27 exploits in our Trace2Inv reproduction. Reentrancy and flash-loan transactions burn far more gas than normal traffic.

properties.statement: Entry points that move value may only be called by an externally owned account, not by a contract.
properties.why: Lowest false-positive rate in our Trace2Inv reproduction at 0.2%. The cost is real: it also blocks legitimate contract integrations such as multisigs and routers.

properties.statement: Privileged functions may only be called by the registered owner address.
properties.formal_sketch: invariant msg.sender == owner for privileged f
properties.why: A missing authorization check is the single most common vulnerability class.

properties.statement: totalSupply must always equal the sum of all balances.
properties.why: Asymmetry between the mint and burn paths surfaces here.

properties.statement: The referenced price may not move by more than a fixed proportion within a single block.
properties.why: Highest false-positive rate in our Trace2Inv reproduction at 22.3% — threshold-based invariants are noisy.

properties.statement: A privileged change may only execute after a minimum delay has elapsed since it was proposed.
properties.why: Admin powers that execute immediately are a rug-pull path.
